findings.title: Roar filter-sensitive setup does not explicitly perform gain-stage Filter Frequency changes

source.quote: Filter Frequency adjusts the filter’s cutoff frequency. If the Pre toggle has been activated, the filter is applied before the Shaper stage. When the Filter Frequency is changed with Pre activated, the filter doesn’t affect the harmonics produced by the shaper.

audit_claims.text: Preserve 007/030 actual selection of nine filters, Freq and Pre contrasts. 007 inspects Resonance/Peak Gain/Morph; add actual respective Resonance, Peak Gain and Morph operations on source-eligible filters, retaining the Resampling exception.
Existing all-nine filter selection, Freq/Pre operations and all-twelve shaper selection remain true

actual_cases.input: Select each of nine filters; inspect Resonance, Peak Gain and Morph; toggle Pre.
actual_cases.expected: Nine types are selectable; Resonance is available except Resampling; Peak and Morph expose their respective controls.

actual_cases.input: Test all nine filter types on S3 with shaper on, contrasting Amount>0, Pre off/on. Establish both filter-sensitive and nonlinear baselines; isolate generated harmonics to distinguish Pre placement. Apply P-AUDIO; if prerequisites are not independently established, outcome remains U.

findings.finding: 007 actually selects all nine filter types, inspects Resonance/Peak Gain/Morph and toggles Pre. 030 tests those types with a shaper, contrasting Amount and Pre off/on, independently established filter-sensitive/nonlinear baselines and generated-harmonic isolation. Neither selected input explicitly changes gain-stage Filter Frequency. A filter-sensitive baseline can be established through type selection or another parameter while Filter Frequency remains fixed. G06 and the B039 assessment therefore overstate those records as actual Freq contrasts. The source documents a Frequency change, but a source operation or positive setup requirement is not itself that selected case action.
findings.counterexample: 007/030 can follow every named operation with gain-stage Filter Frequency left unchanged throughout: filter type selection establishes a responsive filter path and Pre is toggled around productive nonlinear shaping. That does not exercise a Filter Frequency gesture. Case009 analysis Frequency/Width and case012 feedback Filter Frequency/Width are separate controls and cannot supply this gain-stage action.
findings.preserved_true_subsets: Keep all-nine actual filter selection, Pre off/on, filter-sensitive and nonlinear positive baselines, generated-harmonic isolation, actual all-twelve shaper selection and the correctly identified Resonance/Peak/Morph inspection gap. Do not turn all filter actions into missing actions.
findings.requested_minimal_correction: Preserve every frozen R1 audit/source/owner/review byte. In a minimal additive source-audit successor remove or qualify the unsupported actual gain-stage Freq contrast attribution in G06, B039 assessment, their plan counterparts and README summary. Mark the explicit Frequency change as documented-but-not-explicitly-exercised/U, or include it as a bounded future action in the existing group. No new owner requirement or case is mandatory, no archive/catalog duplicate is needed, and no numeric control domain, filter/DSP or output oracle should be added.
findings.verification_expectation: Verify original007/030 full fields and all other original records unchanged. A focused fixture should reject promoting a filter-sensitive baseline, source text or analysis/feedback Frequency operation into an actual gain-stage Filter Frequency change, even if manual plan and derived audit are jointly edited. Preserve null/U/unexecuted and zero credit.
